pr_title: Make ResourceFormatLoaderGDScript perform loading using cache mode
pr_comments:
I'm not entirely sure this won't give problems since `GDScriptCache` will still have the old version if it was there already. OTOH updating the cache might also become an issue because the original one might be freed and try to remove itself from the cache and end up removing the new one instead (since they are keyed by path).

So, I think at minimum this should be pushed to `GDScriptCache`, just pass the cache mode flag when calling. Then maybe we can have a setting in the scripts themselves to tell if they are in the cache. By default they are, but if there's a replacement the `GDScriptCache` singleton can tell the old one that it's not in cache anymore and therefore it should not try to remove itself once it's freed. Not sure if all this is needed, but it feels safer IMO.
We were discussing this on a meeting and we wonder if the bug this solves is related to the bug this other PR is trying to fix: #61870
Other than that, I'll reassess this PR soon with some more care to see if it's valuable on its own (even if it's not needed to fix the bug), since I think it's the case

Fixed some merging conflicts.
Meanwhile, this PR was affected by a few others:
1. #58847
Since auto-reloading of scripts is disabled now by default, performing replacement in files makes the editor pop up a window, listing externally modified files and requesting the user to either reload or resave them. I think that reloading them automatically instead is the correct behavior in such case
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c2eaaef1497f8ad557aea9a14e2b3e0582fcfe54/editor/editor_settings.cpp#L559

2. #62309
Doing `existing->path_cache = String();` in
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c2eaaef1497f8ad557aea9a14e2b3e0582fcfe54/core/io/resource.cpp#L67-L72
leaves `script` with an empty string filename, and causes an error in subsequent `reload` ing as the result
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c2eaaef1497f8ad557aea9a14e2b3e0582fcfe54/editor/plugins/script_editor_plugin.cpp#L964-L971

On the other hand, #61870 does not affect this PR directly, since `ScriptEditor::_reload_scripts` takes care of scripts `last_modified_time` in any case

I also tried to get rid of special cache setting by unrefercing the old script before updating cache with a new one
The `GDScriptCache` has been changed quite a bit to fix cyclic references, so poking @adamscott to see if he has some feedback here.

I just tested the issue and it seems that the latest changes ended up fixing #57870.

This doesn't necessarily renders this PR moot, just that it needs to be updated to consider the changes that occurred.
Closing as the linked bug is fixed, and this PR has merge conflicts and is stale.

issue_context.title: Replace in Files doesn't update file until project is reopened
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0-alpha2

### System information

Windows 11, Nvidia 1050 Ti, Vulkan

### Issue description

The replace all (no undo) doesn't update the file until the project is reopened




https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/53798244/153260894-827f32d2-11b9-4e36-b42c-02224bc635c2.mp4


Edit:
The video doesn't show for me on some browsers, so I uploaded it:

[video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_wHT9iblIjU)


### Steps to reproduce

1 - Open the replace in files menu with Ctrl + Shift + R
2 - Write the word you want to replace
3 - Write the word you want to replace with
4 - Click on Replace....
5 - Down on the Search Results panel, click on Replace all (no undo)
6 - Nothing happens
7 - Re-open the project, the changes are there

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_
comments:
Confirm in Godot 4 alpha 3, same in Find In Files -> Replace.
It actually replaced( writed to file), just not update display.

Could not reproduce in master (1e3919c409).

[Peek 01-12-2022 13-41.webm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/270928/205134307-0fd4d363-819c-492c-8622-94a11000c67e.webm)

I imagine the latest major GDScript changes fixed this issue.
Closing per @adamscott's coment. Please comment if you can still reproduce this on 4.0.beta7 or later.

review_comments: Should we keep it as a side-effect from `script->reload()`?
I assume here that `CACHE_MODE_REUSE` mode was used implicitly before, so this change should be consistent with previous use-cases of `GDScriptCache::get_full_script`
